cap5_start: mid PHYS 356 CAPUT QUINTUM / De statu animae a corpore separata
cap6_start: mid PHYS 372 CAPUT SEXTUM / De hujus mundi fine
titles: CHAPTER FIVE. On the state of the soul separated from the body; death as judgment on Adam's posterity
The state of freed souls is adumbrated figuratively; II duplex common or proper; III common = departure from the visible world
Hermes on death as mutation; body's death when the soul leaves, soul's when God forsakes
IV. Four grades of the common status: divorce, loss of sense, privation of outward acts, defect of consummated glory
V. First plague: the body torn away; Hadrian's lament; Paul would rather be clothed; Tertullian on inferi
VI. Second plague: the sensitive part common with brutes is stripped away; Hebrews 4:12; mind, soul, body
VI continued. Authorities for the division; sensitive part's abolition is the second plague (Prudentius, Plutarch, Antoninus)
VII. Third plague: outward operations cease; Tatian, Tertullian, Nyssen, Bernard, Durandus
VIII. Fourth plague: burning desire for consummated felicity with the resumed body; Bernard; souls under the altar
IX–X. The separated soul is not extinguished; it does not sleep but remembers and knows its lot after judgment
XI. Proper status is duplex: joy of heaven for the pious, torment of gehenna for the impious; no third place
XII–XIII. Joys and torments persist until judgment; no benefit after death; no magical return to earth
XIV. Received opinion: Old-Testament faithful not received into paradise until Christ opened it; limbus patrum
XV–XIX. After Christ opened paradise souls are received at once; fathers differ in speech on heaven vs inferi; no controversy
XX–XXIII. Origen first imported purgatorial fire from Plato; differs from papal thrice; Cap. 5 close
